extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and advanced students working on linear differential equations, conic sections, and classical analytic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and theorems for transforming linear differential equations to reduce order or render them integrable, plus classical constructions and properties of hyperbola/parabola and methods for finding polar reciprocal curves with respect to conics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrability when Q = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose Q = 0, the transformed equation is then integrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text asserts that if after a transformation the coefficient Q vanishes, the transformed equation becomes integrable. The page gives algebraic relations (between P, V, V1, etc.) whose satisfaction yields Q = 0; finding such relations is a way to render the equation integrable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrability by making V = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: By determining Q so as to make V = 0, the transformed would be integrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One can choose or determine transformation parameters (e.g., Q) so that the transformed coefficient V vanishes, which produces an integrable equation. The text notes V = 0 (and analogous vanishing of certain coefficients) reduces the order by one.

rubrics_metrics.name: One integration effected if V = 0 or Q = 0 or W = 0 or W1 = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be observed of the general equations (1), (2), (3), that if V = 0, or Q = 0, or W = 0, W1 = 0, one integration may be effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanishing of any of these named coefficients (V, Q, W, W1) after an appropriate transformation is highlighted as a sufficient condition to perform one integration (i.e., reduce the order by one).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability when coefficient-functions are integer functions
rubrics_metrics.description: But it is when V, V1, etc. Q, Q1, etc. are integer functions of wv, that this method is chiefly applicable; when it may happen that the given equation is susceptible of a series of similar transformations, till it becomes ultimately integrable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method is most useful when the transformed coefficient-functions are integer (in some independent variable or parameter), because then repeated similar transformations may be applied iteratively until the equation becomes integrable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use particular substitutions (v=P=n, v1=P1=2x) to derive conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose then v = P = n, v1 = P1 = 2x. The equations (4) become ... Eliminating all the Q’s, we shall have the equation of condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taking simple integer-valued forms for the transformation parameters (e.g., v and P as integers or linear expressions) yields explicit algebraic conditions between the coefficients (an 'equation of condition') whose satisfaction characterizes transformability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power-series/coefficient-matching method to find admissible constants
rubrics_metrics.description: And supposing V = a + b e + c e^2 + ..., V1 = a' + b' e + c' e^2 + ...; substituting these values, and making the coefficients of the several powers of x zero, we shall find the required relation between the constants that the transformation may be possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represent the relevant coefficient-functions as power series, substitute into the transformation relations, and equate coefficients of powers to obtain algebraic relations among constants; choose constants satisfying those relations to allow the transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate V to transform the other way
rubrics_metrics.description: If we wish to transform the other way, we must eliminate the V’s, and ... with which we must proceed in the same way as before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure is symmetric: one may eliminate different sets of auxiliary coefficients (e.g., eliminating V rather than Q) and repeat the same algebraic procedure to obtain transformability conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family of differential-operator substitutions y = (aD + β) z etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall certainly find all the equations that can be transformed by making y = (Da + β) z, and z = (Da + zn) — ly. And we may make other assumptions for v, v1, P, P1; and may find all the transformable equations corresponding in the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider linear operator substitutions expressed as polynomials in D (differentiation) with constant coefficients; varying these polynomial parameters gives families of transforms and associated algebraic conditions on coefficients for transformability.

rubrics_metrics.description: Put (1) under the form U = Vy + Dφ V1y + D^2 φ' V2y + ... where φ is a function of z; make p = @D; then change V,y into (p + 2b) V,y ... Change now V,y into (p + 3b) V,y, and we find in the same manner DP^' V,y = (p + h)(p + 2b)(p + 3b) V1y, etc. Therefore (5) is changed into ... which may be put under the form ... by making T = V A ... If we can give to @ such a value that T = 0, we shall have ... and the equation will be once integrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a shift operator p = @D and systematically replace V,y by (p + k b) V,y to build factored operator relations; choosing parameters (e.g., @) so that a resulting constructed operator T vanishes is a criterion that produces an integrable reduced equation.

rubrics_metrics.description: Again make r = φD + A = p + rA, 71 = 6D + A = p1 + rA, m = p + A^2, etc.; p = 7 — λ = 7,—A1 = 7^ — Ny ... and we can transform (7) into U = Sy + 78 y + 77 So y + ... where S, S1, etc. are functions of T, T1, etc.; Now if S = 0 in (8), or if we can give to A, A1, etc. and φ such values as make S = 0, we have U = 7S8,y + 77 S1 y + ... and operating with 7^-1 ... the equation is once integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficient-comparison method after substitution U = Xy + X1 Dy + ...
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U = Xy + X1 Dy + X2 D^2 y, and make y = (AD + β) z. By substitution the given equation becomes ... Comparing like terms we have 0A + P AY = X ... These results are perhaps not quite so simple as those obtained by the first method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute a finite linear differential operator applied to y (U expressed in X, X1, ...) and a linear operator substitution for y; equate coefficients of like operator powers to obtain algebraic relations determining the new coefficients and hence transformability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful retention of multiplicative factors in transitions from functions to series
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation ... must be sought for in the circumstances which accompany the transition from a function to its equivalent series when a strict arithmetical equality does not exist between them. ... in symbolical equations which have to be operated upon by multiplication, division, etc., we should never neglect or lay aside any quantity or symbol unless we are certain that the suppression does not assume some unwarranted equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When moving between functions and their series expansions or manipulating symbolic expressions (especially for exponential/imaginary exponentials), retain multiplicative constants and small terms unless rigorous justification exists for their omission; failure to do so leads to paradoxes or incorrect equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a hyperbolic sector into equal parts via mean proportionals (Construction A)
rubrics_metrics.description: From P1 and Pn the extremities of the base P1,Pn of the hyperbolic sector P1OPn, draw straight lines P1Q1 and PnQn parallel to an asymptote, meeting the other asymptote in Q1, Qn; between OQ1 and OQn insert n−2 mean proportionals OQ2, OQ3, ...; through these draw parallels to meet the hyperbola in P2, P3, ..., Pn−1. Then the sector is divided into n−1 equal sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction reduces division to finding mean proportionals along an asymptote. Note: mean proportionals cannot usually be constructed by straightedge-and-compass except in special cases, but they can be computed numerically from the algebraic relations given (equations (8)-(10)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum inscribed polygon in a hyperbolic segment: tangent parallelism condition (Construction B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P1P2...Pm is the maximum polygon inscribed in the segment P1Pn, the tangent at Pi must be parallel to the chord P_{i−1}P_{i+1}. This leads to algebraic conditions (e.g., equation (13)). Construction: find points Pi as in (A) and join them to get the maximum polygon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extremality condition for an inscribed polygon is that each tangent at a vertex be parallel to the opposite chord; use the sector-division points from (A) to locate vertices of the maximal polygon numerically or constructively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum circumscribed polygon about a hyperbolic segment via tangents (Construction C)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the points P1, P2, ..., Pn found as in (A), draw tangents to the hyperbola; their intersections form the polygon of m+1 sides circumscribed about the segment. If chosen appropriately this is the minimum polygon circumscribed about the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct tangents at the precomputed contact points; the polygon formed by their intersections is the minimal circumscribed polygon corresponding to the maximal inscribed polygon derived earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angular points of minimum circumscribed polygon lie on a concentric similar hyperbola (Proposition D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The angular points of a minimum polygon circumscribed about a segment of a hyperbola are situated in a concentric similar hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a structural/geometric property used to relate the circumscribed polygon's vertices to a similar hyperbola centered at the same center as the original hyperbola; use to reduce or relate constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality between maximal inscribed and minimal circumscribed polygons (Propositions E and F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P,R,... is the minimum polygon circumscribed about segment P1Pn, and R,R_{n−1} are joined, the polygon R,R,... is the maximum polygon of m−1 sides inscribed in the segment of the concentric similar hyperbola. The sides of a maximum polygon inscribed in a segment of a hyperbola touch a concentric similar hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a direct dual correspondence: vertices of one extremal polygon correspond to tangent-contact points of the other, and vice versa. This provides practical construction and characterization strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction for maximum polygon in a parabolic segment (Construction b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the chord (base) P1Pn of the parabolic segment into n−1 equal parts Q1, Q2, ..., Qn−1, and through these draw straight lines parallel to a diameter of the parabola meeting the arc in P2, P3, ..., Pn−1; joining P1P2...Pn yields the maximum polygon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For parabolic segments, the equal partition of the base (not geometric mean proportionals) yields the contact points for the maximal inscribed polygon; this is a simpler construction than for the hyperbola.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum circumscribed polygon for parabola via tangents at constructed points (Construction c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Having found the points P2, P3, ... as in (b), tangents at these points meet to form the minimum polygon of m+1 sides circumscribed about the parabolic segment P1Pn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous duality and construction method as in the hyperbola case, but using equally spaced base partitions; tangents at those points give the minimal circumscribed polygon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angular points of minimum circumscribed polygon of parabola lie on an equal parabola (Proposition d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The angular points of a minimum polygon circumscribed about a segment of a parabola are situated in an equal parabola, and the two parabolas have their principal axes in the same straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural property parallels the hyperbola case and is useful in deducing geometric relations between inscribed and circumscribed polygons for parabolic segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality for parabolic polygons (Propositions e and f)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P, R, ... is the minimum circumscribed polygon about a parabolic segment, then joining certain vertices yields a maximum inscribed polygon in the related parabolic segment of the reciprocal parabola; sides of a maximum polygon inscribed in a parabolic segment touch an equal parabola with the same principal axes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the analogous dual relationships for parabolas: extremal inscribed and circumscribed polygons correspond via tangency and equality-of-axis relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and equation of the polar of a point with respect to a conic
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line from a given point P meets a conic in Q and Q' and P and P' are conjugate harmonic points w.r.t. Q and Q', then the locus of P' is a straight line called the polar of P; the explicit equation is (2): (A a1 + B y1 + D) x + (B a1 + C y1 + E) y + D a1 + E y1 + F = 0 (notation as in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the polar by substituting the chord-tangent relations into the conic equation and eliminating the roots. The polar is a linear relation in coordinates whose coefficients depend on the conic's coefficients and P's coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity of polars (Theorem III)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the polar of a given point P passes through another point R, reciprocally the polar of R will pass through P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fundamental reciprocal property means that incidence between a point and a polar line is symmetric; it is the algebraic underpinning of the pole-polar correspondence used in constructions and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar reciprocal curves definition (III)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any two curves PQR and P'Q'R' in the plane of a conic section are such that the points of the one are the poles of tangents applied to the other at corresponding points, then the curves are polar reciprocals with respect to the conic director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may treat either curve as the envelope of polars of the other's points, or as the locus of poles of the other's tangents. This is a test and construction device for producing reciprocal curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent-ordinate parallelism (Theorem IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A tangent applied to one of the curves at any point is parallel to the ordinates of the diameter of the director which passes through the corresponding point of its reciprocal curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this relation to find directions of tangents on reciprocal curves: the tangent direction corresponds to the ordinate-direction of a conjugate diameter through the corresponding point on the reciprocal curve (specializing to perpendicularity when the director is a circle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of a reciprocal curve with respect to a circle (Method V)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the director is a circle of unit radius about the origin, the coordinates of the point of the reciprocal curve corresponding to a tangent at (x',y') are the reciprocals of the segments which the tangent intercepts on the axes; explicit equation given as (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the tangent at a point of the given curve, find its intercepts on the chosen coordinate axes, take reciprocals of those intercepts (after normalization), and these reciprocals are the coordinates of the corresponding point of the reciprocal curve. The method yields an explicit algebraic formula for the reciprocal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabola vs center criterion (VI.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When B^2 − AC = 0 the curve (5) evidently passes through the origin. Hence when one of the curves is a parabola, the reciprocal curve passes through the centre of the director. Conversely when the curve passes through the centre of the director, the other curve is a parabola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the discriminant B^2 − AC to detect a parabola; such a condition predicts whether the reciprocal passes through the director's center, and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptote / tangent perpendicularity conditions (VI.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When D' − AF = 0, the curve (4) touches the axis of x, and (5) is a hyperbola having an asymptote parallel to the axis of y. Hence the asymptotes of one of the curves are perpendicular to the tangents drawn to the other from the centre of the director, and the converse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear relations among coefficients (involving D', A, F, etc.) imply geometric relations between tangents and asymptotes of reciprocal curves; use coefficient equalities to infer perpendicularity or parallelism of special lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axis-parallelism condition (VI.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When B = 0 and D = 0, or B = 0 and E = 0, we have DE − FB = 0; hence when the centre of the director is on an axis of one of the reciprocal curves, the axes of those curves are parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zeroing certain mixed-coefficient terms implies axis alignment or parallelism between the reciprocal curves; check these coefficient vanishings to deduce axis-direction relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tangent/normal axis interpretation (VI.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: When D = 0 and F = 0, the axes of x and y are evidently a tangent and normal to the curve (4); in this case the equation of the reciprocal curve is ... which denotes a parabola having its axis parallel to the axis of y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting coordinate axes as tangent and normal at a point simplifies reciprocal equations; certain coefficient vanishings correspond to taking axes aligned with geometric features (tangent/normal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentric-curves reciprocal lengths condition (VI.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When B = 0, C = 0, D = 0, and F = 0, the equations of the reciprocal curves are A x^2 + 2 E y = 0 and E x^2 − 2 A y = 0; hence when one of the curves is concentric with the director, the axes of the reciprocal curves coincide in direction, and the lengths of the coincident axes are reciprocals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special coefficient vanishings correspond to concentric arrangements; this yields a reciprocal proportionality in semiaxes lengths of the reciprocal curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar of the centre coincidence property (VI.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The polar of the centre of the director taken with respect to one of the reciprocal curves coincides with the polar of the centre of the other curve taken with respect to the director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the explicit polar formula to check that the polars of centres coincide, giving a check or construction tool linking the centres of reciprocal curves and the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center-at-focus => reciprocal circle condition (VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: When FB − DE = 0, and FA − D'*= FC − E', this equation becomes ... and the reciprocal curve is a circle. Hence when the centre of the director coincides with a focus of one of the curves the reciprocal curve is a circle; the centres of the three curves lie in the same straight line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special algebraic equalities among coefficients signal that placing the director's center at a focus of the given conic produces a circular reciprocal; this is a geometric design criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similar-conics/harmonic-pencil intersection theorem (VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two conic sections are similar, their polar reciprocals intersect on two straight lines which pass through the pole of the straight line joining the centres of the two given curves; and those conjugate common secants together with the polars of these centres form a harmonic pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this theorem to deduce intersection loci and harmonic relations among lines associated with families of similar conics and their reciprocals; it provides a projective-geometric criterion for concurrency and harmonic division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentric conics reciprocal-common-secant property (VIII continuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The polar reciprocals of any two concentric conic sections have the centre of the director for a point of intersection of conjugate common secants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conics share the same centre, their reciprocals share conjugate secant-line intersections through the director centre; useful for identifying symmetry and shared geometric loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: General method for polar reciprocal with respect to arbitrary conic (Equation 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: To find the polar reciprocal of any curve of the second degree with respect to any other curve of the second degree taken as director, equate the tangent of the given curve at (x',y') with the polar of the putative reciprocal point (x,y) with respect to the director and eliminate to obtain equation (10) — an explicit algebraic relation for the reciprocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve the linear system equating tangent and polar expressions, introduce auxiliaries for the second members, and eliminate to obtain the reciprocal's equation. Equation (10) is the general algebraic formula to compute the reciprocal curve for an arbitrary quadratic director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-parabola specialization and parabolic reciprocal properties (XI & XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the director is a parabola (choose coefficients accordingly), equation (10) reduces to (12), which differs from the circle-director case; e.g., when B'^2 − A C = 0 the reciprocal curve has an asymptote parallel to the axis of x, so parabolic polar reciprocals have distinct properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the director is a parabola, substitute the canonical coefficient values into the general reciprocal formula to obtain the specialized reciprocal equation (12) and use it to deduce parabolic-specific geometric relations (asymptotes, axes relations).
